properties.statement:
THE SERVED-SURFACE GATE DEFAULTS TO `target/debug/reflow2-mcp` AND SAYS "ALL 149 TOOLSNAPS MATCH" AGAINST WHATEVER STALE BUILD IS SITTING THERE. A green from it is evidence about a binary nobody promised was current.

MEASURED 2026-08-16, on my own change and by accident. I edited a `#[tool(description = …)]`, rebuilt RELEASE, ran `python3 tools/toolsnap.py`, and was told the surface was unchanged. It was not: the new sentence was present in the release binary (1 occurrence via `strings`) and ABSENT from the committed snapshot, which still held the old description. `tools/toolsnap.py:140` sets `--bin` default to `target/debug/reflow2-mcp`; debug was an hour older than release (11:27 vs 12:27). Rebuilding debug and re-running immediately reported `TOOLSNAP DRIFT (1)`.

⚠️ THE SNAPSHOT DOES CONTAIN THE DESCRIPTION — this is not a scope limitation. `tools/toolsnaps/create_node.json` carries a `description` field and the file's own docstring says "the whole served object is snapshotted — name, description, inputSchema". So the comparison is right and the INPUT to it is wrong.

⭐ THE SHAPE IS THE ONE THIS PROJECT KEEPS FINDING: a check that cannot fail reporting a pass. Same class as `propose_heal`'s vacuous zero fixed hours earlier, the piped-gate exit code, and `sync` reporting `in_step` over unexported work. Here the gate whose entire job is to notice a changed surface reported an unchanged one BECAUSE the surface it read had not been rebuilt.

✅ CORRECTED SAME DAY, AND THE CORRECTION LOWERS THE SEVERITY. The first version of this fact said it was NOT ESTABLISHED whether CI had the same hole, because `.github/workflows/ci.yml:142` runs `toolsnap.py` with no `--bin` and so takes the same default. IT DOES NOT: `ci.yml:93` runs `cargo build -p reflow2-mcp` — a DEBUG build — in the same job, before the toolsnap step. So CI compares a freshly built debug binary every time and was never exposed. ⇒ THIS IS A LOCAL-DEVELOPER DEFECT ONLY, and specifically it bites the person following the RELEASE PROCEDURE, which instructs a release build and leaves debug behind.

AND THAT IS ALSO WHY THE FIX MUST NOT CHANGE THE DEFAULT to `target/release`: CI builds debug and would then compare a binary that does not exist there. FIXED 2026-08-16 by `chg:the-surface-gate-says-which-binary-it-read` — every verdict now names the binary and its build time, and warns when any `crates/**/src/*.rs` is newer than it. mtime is a weak signal alone (git operations can leave sources older than a build, which is why the launch wrapper hashes content instead), but it is only ever used to ADD a warning and never to suppress one, so a false negative costs nothing that was not already lost.

ANOTHER GATE WITH THE SAME DEFAULT, seen 2026-09-28 in the dev_reflow2 hub session. tools/reflow2_check.py resolves its binary as $REFLOW2_BIN, then target/debug, then target/release, then PATH (lines 58-68). On a machine whose debug build was 0.73.0 and whose release build was 0.74.0, the local run refused the 0.74.0 export ("you are running 0.73.0, which is BEHIND it"). The refusal was correct and loud, and the run passed with REFLOW2_BIN pointed at the release build. The class is unchanged: a local gate prefers a build nobody necessarily rebuilt over the one just built.
properties.value: {"measured":"2026-08-16, reflow2's own repo, found while changing a tool description","symptom":"toolsnap.py reported ALL 149 MATCH while the committed snapshot held the OLD description and the new one was in the release binary","mechanism":"tools/toolsnap.py:140 defaults --bin to target/debug/reflow2-mcp; debug was an hour stale (11:27 vs release 12:27)","proof":"rebuilt debug, re-ran, got TOOLSNAP DRIFT (1) immediately","not_a_scope_limit":"the snapshot DOES contain description; the docstring says the whole served object is snapshotted","class":"a check that cannot fail reporting a pass","ci_ESTABLISHED_and_safe":"ci.yml:93 runs cargo build -p reflow2-mcp (debug) in the same job BEFORE the toolsnap step at :142, so CI always compares a fresh binary and was never exposed - this corrects the first version of this fact, which left it unchecked","blast_radius":"local developers only, and specifically whoever follows the release procedure, which builds release and leaves debug behind","why_the_default_must_stay_debug":"CI builds debug; defaulting to release would point CI at a binary it never built","fixed_by":"chg:the-surface-gate-says-which-binary-it-read - every verdict names the binary and its build time and warns when any crates/**/src/*.rs is newer"}
